best_idea: A quest is a state predicate checked once per turn over the world, with a claim set per player so a repeatable reward is paid once; a world-first objective is a separate unique flag that the first qualifying player claims (random tie-break among the same turn's qualifiers), and every reward lands in one history ledger.
decision_why: The unique world-first flag and the claim set fit zones-as-data and the one-ledger rule; adapt by running the check on server-verified events instead of a turn sweep and by making the unique flag a required zone field; reject compounding interest on quest rewards, which is progression, not a quest.
acceptance: In a zone with a world-first objective, when two players reach the server-verified threshold in the same tick, exactly one is recorded as first holder and gets one ledger row while the other gets nothing; a repeatable objective pays each player once, not on every tick after the threshold.
